claims.text: Web Summit's organisers announced in September 2015 that the event would move from Dublin to Lisbon from 2016.
claims.quote: The Web Summit in Dublin will be no more from 2016 with the organisers confirming that the event is to up sticks and move to Lisbon

claims.text: The organisers cited infrastructure as one of their reasons for leaving Dublin (as Silicon Republic reports it).
claims.quote: with the organisation citing infrastructure as one of the reasons for its decision

claims.text: Founder Paddy Cosgrave said the move was made to take the next step in international growth.
claims.quote: We are going because we want to take the next step on our journey to international growth.

claims.text: The article reports a venue in Lisbon with capacity for more than 80,000 attendees, and expected more than 30,000 people at the 2015 edition in Dublin's RDS.
claims.quote: This November, the Web Summit expects more than 30,000 people to attend the event in the RDS.

claims.text: On the first Lisbon edition's opening night in 2016, ticket holders were left outside the venue.
claims.quote: People who paid thousands for tickets left waiting outside Web Summit

claims.text: TheJournal.ie reported that Web Summit's website confirmed the 2016 edition sold out, with 53,056 people attending.
claims.quote: The Web Summit website confirms that the event is sold out with 53,056 people attending.

claims.text: As TheJournal.ie recalls it, the organiser cited unreliable Wi-Fi at the RDS, traffic management, public transport and hotel costs as factors in leaving Dublin.
claims.quote: he cited unreliable WiFi at the RDS, issues with traffic management, public transport and hotel costs as influential factors

claims.text: In 2016 the late-late ticket prices ran from 1,000 euros (exhibition floor only) to 3,000 (General Attendee), 4,245 (Premium) and 5,245 (Platinum).
claims.quote: Late late ticket prices started at €1,000 for exhibition floor only and rose to €3,000 for a General Attendee, €4,245 for Premium and €5,245 for the Platinum ticket.

claims.text: In November 2017 Portugal's Prime Minister criticised a Web Summit dinner held at the National Pantheon in Lisbon as 'offensive'; the organiser apologised.
claims.quote: Paddy Cosgrave has apologised after Portugal’s Prime Minister criticised him for holding an “offensive” summit dinner at Lisbon’s National Pantheon

claims.text: The Prime Minister said laws would be amended to prevent the Pantheon being used for similar events (as TheJournal.ie reports it).
claims.quote: Laws will be amended to prevent the Pantheon from being used for similar events in the future, according to Costa

claims.text: In August 2018 Web Summit's founder withdrew an invitation to Marine Le Pen to the 2018 Lisbon edition, after earlier defending it.
claims.quote: has withdrawn an invite for French far-right leader Marine Le Pen to its annual tech conference later this year, after earlier defending the decision to invite her

claims.text: The founder gave as his reason that her presence would be disrespectful to the host country and to some attendees.
claims.quote: her presence is disrespectful in particular to our host country

claims.text: The 2018 Lisbon edition was scheduled for 5 to 8 November.
claims.quote: which will be held in the Portuguese capital from 5-8 November

claims.text: Web Summit's CEO and co-founder resigned on 21 October 2023 with immediate effect, saying his personal comments had become a distraction from the event.
claims.quote: I am resigning as CEO of Web Summit with immediate effect.

claims.text: Google and Meta withdrew from the 2023 edition, following Intel and Siemens, after the CEO's remarks about Western support for Israel (as RTE reports it).
claims.quote: tech giants Google and Meta became the latest companies to withdraw from the Web Summit

claims.text: Web Summit said the 2023 edition in Lisbon would go ahead as planned.
claims.quote: Web Summit 2023 in Lisbon will go ahead as planned.

claims.text: Web Summit appointed Katherine Maher, previously chief executive of Wikipedia, as its new chief executive, two weeks before the 2023 Lisbon conference.
claims.quote: Web Summit has appointed Katherine Maher as its new chief executive

claims.text: RTE reported that the departing CEO continued to own 81% of the company.
claims.quote: Paddy Cosgrave continues to own 81% of the company.

claims.text: In January 2024 Web Summit's chief executive Katherine Maher announced she would step down on 1 March 2024, three months after taking the role, to become chief executive of NPR.
claims.quote: stepping down from the company just three months after replacing cofounder Paddy Cosgrave

claims.text: She stays on as non-executive chair of the executive board, and the company's first conference in Doha, Qatar was to be led under her before she stepped down.
claims.quote: leading the events company through its first conference in Doha, Qatar

claims.text: The company named Craig Becker, its chief events officer, as an executive board member.
claims.quote: The company also named Craig Becker, Web Summit’s chief events officer, as an executive board member on Wednesday.

claims.text: The 2020 flagship edition was held online; TechCrunch wrote this on 2 December 2020 while it was taking place.
claims.quote: The flagship Web Summit event is currently taking place as an online conference.

claims.text: In December 2020 Web Summit had already announced plans to hold its flagship event in person in Lisbon in November 2021.
claims.quote: Web Summit has already announced plans to hold its flagship event as an in-person conference in November 2021 in Lisbon, Portugal.

claims.text: In December 2020 Web Summit said its global expansion would include an event in Brazil, with Rio de Janeiro or Porto Alegre under consideration as the location.
claims.quote: an event in Brazil; Rio de Janeiro or Porto Alegre are currently being considered as the location

claims.text: The last in-person Web Summit before the pandemic, in November 2019, had 70,469 attendees (as the company's figure is reported).
claims.quote: The last in-person Web Summit event, which took place in November 2019, had 70,469 attendees.

claims.text: Web Summit relocated to Lisbon in 2016 under a deal with the Portuguese government, with a 10-year agreement to host its flagship event there.
claims.quote: It relocated to Lisbon in 2016 under a deal with the Portuguese government.

claims.text: The online-only 2020 edition attracted 104,000 people.
claims.quote: attracting 104,000 people

claims.text: The group that operates Web Summit reported 2019 revenue of 47.9 million euros.
claims.quote: Revenues at the group that operates the Web Summit rose to €47.9 million in 2019.

claims.text: For the 2021 Lisbon edition more than 40,000 people were expected in person, which organisers said was sold out, with Covid restrictions in place.
claims.quote: more than 40,000 people expected to converge on the Portuguese capital

claims.text: Web Summit announced an event in Rio de Janeiro, the first Web Summit outside Europe, planned for May of the following year.
claims.quote: Tech conference Web Summit is expanding to South America, with plans to hold the event in Rio de Janeiro in May next year.

claims.text: Web Summit's chief executive said the event was committed to Rio for at least three years, with an option to extend.
claims.quote: the event was committed to Rio for at least three years, with an option to extend that further

claims.text: Rio's mayor said the city would not put in any direct money or sponsorship, with Senac as the main sponsor.
claims.quote: the city would not be putting in any direct money or sponsorship of the event, with Senac acting as the main sponsor

claims.text: The Irish Times reported a new 10-year deal between the company and the Portuguese government keeping Web Summit in Lisbon until at least 2028, worth 110 million euros.
claims.quote: The Web Summit will remain in Lisbon until at least 2028 under a new €110 million deal

claims.text: The deal followed a tender with offers from more than 20 major cities.
claims.quote: This follows a tender process involving offers from more than 20 major cities

claims.text: Under the deal the company is paid 11 million euros a year, and it includes a major expansion of the existing venue.
claims.quote: The new 10-year deal will see the company paid €11 million annually and includes a major expansion of the existing venue
